children: 0853 GMT - The pickup in inflation in Indonesia is not expected to significantly pressure Bank Indonesia to resume rate hikes, especially as the trade balance returned to a surplus, Barclays economist Brian Tan says in a note. Indonesia's inflation rebounded to 3.19% in August from 2.88% in July, while the trade balance returned to a surplus in July after two consecutive months of deficits. The return of a trade surplus is expected to ease concerns over import-driven growth and rupiah pressure, he says. Bank Indonesia is projected to maintain policy rates on hold through 2026 if rupiah pressures stay contained, while previously anticipated rate cuts in 2027 are no longer expected, he adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0848 GMT - U.K. 30-year government bond yields, or gilt yields jump to their highest level since 1998, but this could offer investors attractive carry opportunity, Natixis strategists say in a note. "Curve steepness in the long end reflects structural drivers like quantitative tightening, heavy long-end supply and regulatory change, as much as macro fundamentals, creating carry opportunities at current yield levels," they say. The U.K. budget statement due on October 28, could be a key inflection point as the fiscal watchdog, the Office for Budget Responsibility, is due to deliver an assessment on fiscal credibility, the strategists say. U.K. 30-year gilt yields climb 10 basis points to 5.886%, having earlier hit 5.893%, their highest since 1998, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0840 GMT - China's new housing reforms could weigh on construction activity, says BofA Securities in a note. It is encouraging that manufacturing activity improved in August from July, BofA points out. "In particular, the notable rebound in new orders suggests a better near-term recovery outlook, likely led by large enterprises," it says. However, construction activity continued to remain weak. BofA says the housing reform announced last week, which requires future residential projects to be sold as completed homes or only after structural completion, could reduce developers' capital turnover. This may further weigh on property-related construction activity in the future, BofA says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0827 GMT - Faster tightening is the BOJ's most immediate response to the increase in JGB yields, Capital Economics says. That can reduce lingering concerns about inflation, but it would probably take a further surge in yields to convince the BOJ to step up bond purchases again. The 10-year JGB yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996, but the move has been less abrupt than at the start of the year. Accordingly, the odds of major financial dislocations are small, says CE's Marcel Thieliant. Soaring yields could stress insurers and pension funds, but higher long-term borrowing costs have limited impact on economic activity as most private-sector debt in Japan consists of loans. And since JGB moves are part of a global selloff, authorities may see attempts to tame yields as futile. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0812 GMT - The Bank of Japan is likely to hike or intervene in the coming weeks, given the yen's underperformance, RBC Capital Markets' Abbas Keshvani says in commentary. The yen has underperformed over the last month, undoing most of BOJ's intervention in recent months. A yen recovery will require an aggressive hiking cycle, but the central bank is unlikely to jeopardize growth in such a manner, he says. "Instead, they will likely hike enough to prevent excessive yen weakness until stability in JGBs next year can usher in a currency recovery," he adds. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0803 GMT - Volatility in government bond yields is expected to be a major driver of risk asset prices, BCA research's Felix Vezina-Poirier says in a note. Sovereign bond yields have climbed to multiyear highs due to inflation concerns given high oil prices. "The level of yields matters less for equities than how quickly rates move, making implied rates volatility the more useful gauge of equity risk." Nonetheless, the U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's speech last week signalling readiness to act to contain inflation should keep rates volatility fairly contained, Vezina-Poirier says. Ten-year U.S. Treasury yields rise 2.4 basis points to last trade at 4.782%, having hit 4.786%, their highest since January 2025, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0800 GMT - India's central bank won't be able to look entirely past the rise in inflation, UOB economists say as they pencil in two back-to-back 25bp rate hikes starting from December. Under UOB's baseline projections, headline inflation could breach the upper bound of the RBI's 2%-6% tolerance band by fiscal 3Q and remain above 6% until early 1Q. That would imply negative real rates that may necessitate tighter monetary conditions to constrain demand-driven inflation, says UOB's Jester Koh. While price pressures remain highly concentrated in the food category for now, the RBI is still likely to act given the potential influence on household inflation expectations, which have strengthened meaningfully since the start of 2026. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0745 GMT - Shares in U.K. home builders fell after August's Nationwide House Price Index showed the market was still finding its footing. Analysts at RBC Capital Markets note that annual growth peaked at 4.7% in December 2024, faded through 2025, and has settled since into a 1.4% to 2.2% range through most of 2026. "The market is not falling, but it is not flying either. It is a market in a holding pattern, circling and waiting for the right conditions to land," RBC says. Vistry is down 3.7%, with Berkeley down 3.2% and Crest Nicholson down 2.9%. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)

0734 GMT - Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, climb to multiyear highs due to inflation concerns as the U.S.-Iran war persists. Efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have not succeeded, raising fears about prolonged oil supply disruptions and high energy costs. U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh also warned on Friday about inflation risks. Ten-year gilt yields rise to 5.224%, their highest level since 2008, LSEG data show. Thirty-year gilt yields rise to their highest since 1998 at 5.871%.(miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0729 GMT - The U.K. housing market is grinding along rather than powering ahead, RBC Capital Markets analysts Anthony Codling and Oliver Dyson say in a note. According to the Nationwide House Price Index for August, annual prices grew 1.6% with a modest 0.2% month-on-month uptick, RBC says. On a non-seasonally adjusted basis the average U.K. home now costs 275,465 pounds, below July's 276,581 pounds, thus underlining just how flat conditions really are, RBC says. Geopolitical tensions are keeping energy prices and market interest rates elevated and cast a shadow over consumer confidence and mortgage affordability, the analysts say. Although wage growth continues to outpace house-price growth, so affordability is improving gradually, higher mortgage rates are eating into those gains, the analysts say. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)

0721 GMT - Japan's real gross domestic product growth for the April-June quarter is likely to be revised upward to 0.4% on an on-quarter basis and to 1.6% in annualized terms, as Ministry of Finance figures indicate stronger-than-expected capital expenditures, says Daiwa Securities economist Kento Minami. That compares with initial readings of +0.3% and +1.1%, respectively. Revised GDP data is due Sept. 8. The reading will "likely confirm that while domestic demand lost some momentum from the previous quarter, Japan's broader growth trajectory remains largely intact," Minami says.(megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

0712 GMT - Bitcoin edges lower due to increased expectations of the U.S. Federal Reserve raising interest rates in the coming months. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh last week said that inflation risks remain and that the Fed is prepared to take action to contain them. Markets increase rate-hike expectations as a result and now price a 65% possibility of the Fed raising rates on Sept. 16. Bitcoin falls 0.1% to 78,746, remaining below the key $80,000 level, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
